ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{1}{x}$ intersects with the graph of the direct proportion function $y=x$ at points A and C. $AB\perp x$-axis and $CD\perp x$-axis, with the perpendicular feet at points B and D, respectively. What is the area of the quadrilateral ABCD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solving the system of equations for the two functions gives \(\begin{cases}y=\frac{1}{x}, \\ y=x, \end{cases}\) which results in \(\begin{cases}x=1, \\ y=1, \end{cases}\) or \(\begin{cases}x=-1, \\ y=-1. \end{cases}\)

\(\therefore A(1, 1), C(-1, -1).\)

\(\because AB\perp x\) axis, \(CD\perp x\) axis,

\(\therefore B(1, 0), D(-1, 0),\)

\(\therefore BD=2, AB=CD=1.\)

\(\because AB\perp BD, CD\perp BD\)

\(\therefore AB\parallel CD\)

\(\therefore\) Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,

\(\therefore\) The area of quadrilateral ABCD \(=AB\cdot BD=1\times 2=\boxed{2}\).

\textbf{Solution:} Solving the system of equations for the two functions gives \(\begin{cases}y=\frac{1}{x}, \\ y=x, \end{cases}\) which results in \(\begin{cases}x=1, \\ y=1, \end{cases}\) or \(\begin{cases}x=-1, \\ y=-1. \end{cases}\)

\(\therefore A(1, 1), C(-1, -1).\)

\(\because AB\perp x\) axis, \(CD\perp x\) axis,

\(\therefore B(1, 0), D(-1, 0),\)

\(\therefore BD=2, AB=CD=1.\)

\(\because AB\perp BD, CD\perp BD\)

\(\therefore AB\parallel CD\)

\(\therefore\) Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,

\(\therefore\) The area of quadrilateral ABCD \(=AB\cdot BD=1\times 2=\boxed{2}\)
